entry: A05 — The group whose divisibility is actually asserted
statement: "la partie discrète de H¹(K, A) est divisible" (43/120) belongs to G.'s local duality over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field (Shafarevich, Ogg; Bégueri, Mém. entry: A18 — Component-group duality is asserted alongside cohomological duality
statement: Known: "π_0(A) et π_0(B) duaux" (43/117) is Grothendieck's pairing on component groups (SGA 7, IX §11): perfect for perfect residue fields (T. Suzuki 2020, after McCallum and Bertapelle), not in general for imperfect ones (Bertapelle-Bosch 2000).

entry: A21 — The biduality scratch leaves a completion map to identify
statement: The Δ² biduality scratch with "complété", "compact" (43/116); local, reading doubts recorded in the note.

entry: D02 — Algebraically closed vanishing and base extension
statement: Known: H^i(k, F) = 0 for i > 0 over an algebraically closed field, and base extension of sheaf Ext (43/094); standard (every fppf cover of Spec k has a section).

entry: D08 — The first duality comparison has a written exclusion
statement: "isom si G affine sans … composantes G_a" (43/100) and "sans composantes abéliennes" (43/130); scope restrictions of the duality as written; the curve case is Artin-Milne (Invent. Math. 1976) and Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, III.

statement: Edition: on 43/117 the upper box writes H¹(K, B) as a product, while the diagram below gives only an extension of Ext¹(𝒜′⁰, Q/Z) by Ext(U, Q/Z) terms; no section is written.

entry: D20 — The fundamental comparison is composition with a proposed trace
statement: Known: the trace-composition recipe Rf_*G → Rf_*(Sσ[i]) → σ[i] for duality on a curve (43/130) is the shape of flat duality for curves (Artin-Milne 1976; Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems, III); the trace γ is the step G. leaves.

statement: Self-duality of the Jacobian at infinitesimal order and the cote 44 Theorem 4 (43/133); part of @1146.

statement: Known: the largest α_p^n subgroup of A and the largest α_p^n quotient of _pA are dual (43/133): Oda 1969 (Dieudonné-module duality; the a-number of A equals that of its dual); see @1420, @1428.

statement: The reused homotopy typescript's conjecture on Df and Δ (43/101); duplicate of @1430 (Atiyah, Thom complexes).

entry: P02 — Algebraization, projectivity and punctured Picard groups are separate questions
statement: Known: algebraization over an excellent ("bon") henselian ring, and descent of projectivity from the completion, follow from Artin approximation (M. Artin 1969) with ampleness read on the closed fibre (EGA III 4.7.1); punctured Picard groups: SGA 2, XI-XIII; Boutot, Schéma de Picard local (LNM 632, 1978). See @1447 for Michel Hua's project's 57-analytic-pic-completion-criterion.

entry: P05 — Sheafification and torsor representability are explicit hypotheses
statement: Known: Pic as the fppf sheafification and torsor representability (57/275-276): FGA (TDTE V, VI); Kleiman, The Picard scheme (2005); see @1448.

entry: P06 — The weaker quotient-existence expectation stays open on the page
statement: Known in algebraic spaces: G.'s "Il semble … Au concours !" (57/277) on the quotient Pic/Pic^τ needs only flatness and closedness: quotients by flat closed subgroups of finite presentation exist as algebraic spaces (M. Artin 1974, Cor. 6.3); as schemes, Raynaud 1967 and Anantharaman 1973. See @1448.

entry: P09 — The product formula depends on universal hypotheses
statement: The Picard exact sequence for g: X → Y with O_Y ≅ g_*O_X universally, split by a section (57/283); standard (Kleiman 2005).

entry: P10 — Fixed parts require care with the action and with scheme structure
statement: Fixed parts under the diagonal action, "schéma non ramifié" (57/284, 286); local.

entry: P11 — The final openness proposition has missing local dependencies
statement: Known: Pic^τ is an open subfunctor of finite presentation, closed under projectivity and geometrically integral fibres (57/314): SGA 6, XIII (Kleiman) Th. 4.7; Kleiman 2005, §6. The cited criteria (viii′ b′), (viii e): @1469.

entry: E02 — Two different Hodge terms drive the proposed asymmetry
statement: Known phenomena of characteristic p: Hodge asymmetry dim t_{A′}^Γ − dim (t_A)′^Γ of either sign and nonreduced Picard schemes (57/287-288): Igusa 1955; Serre 1958 (Mexico); Mumford, Pathologies of modular algebraic surfaces (1961).

entry: E03 — The four pathologies are announced outcomes, not four completed examples
statement: The four announced pathologies, "Comme conséquence, on aura des exemples" (57/288); folded into #1220.

entry: E04 — The specialization construction distinguishes integral divisibility from rational identification
statement: Known phenomenon: p-divisibility of homomorphisms need not generize (57/289-290); for example F² is ±p on a supersingular curve over F_{p²} with π = ±p and not divisible by p on the ordinary generic fibre; prime to p the cokernel of specialization is torsion-free. Duplicate of @1451 (Michel Hua's project's 57-ns-p-divisibility-generization).

entry: E07 — The first-order diagrams need map-level interpretation
statement: First-order deformation diagrams, Im(uμ) ⊂ Im(v) and the μ_2-Picard sequence (57/294, 297); local, with the reading doubts recorded in the note.

entry: E08 — Continuity of Néron–Severi torsion is distinct from rank continuity
statement: Known: "Continuité de la torsion de N.S." (57/309(f), 310(7), 311): prime to p, NS_tors ⊗ Z_ℓ = H²(X, Z_ℓ(1))_tors is locally constant in smooth proper families (smooth and proper base change); the p-part jumps (Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2, Bombieri-Mumford 1976); jumps of the rank and the torsion-free cokernel after inverting p: Maulik-Poonen (Duke 2012), Prop. 3.6.

entry: E09 — Variation and correspondence representability remain differently qualified
statement: Known: constancy of α + μ + λ and the "connu" inequality 2α + μ ≤ 2α′ + μ′ under specialization (57/313): semicontinuity of abelian and toric ranks (SGA 7, IX §2); the correspondence question answered "Oui, par Raynaud" (Raynaud, Spécialisation du foncteur de Picard, 1970).

entry: E10 — Extension of an algebraically trivial bundle has two obligations
statement: Extension of an algebraically trivial L_t across a trait with algebraically trivial special restriction (57/314-315): known in the projective case with geometrically integral fibres (Pic^τ closed: SGA 6, XIII 4.7; Kleiman 2005, §6); folded into #1219.

entry: C03 — Independent restrictions obstruct projectivity of the second pushout
statement: Known type of example: a pinching P^r ⊔_Y P^r with only trivial line bundles is proper and not projective while its normalization is (57/302); the check runs through Z² → Pic(Y) and the unit-gluing parameter (Ferrand, Conducteur, descente et pincement, 2003); local.

entry: C05 — A bounded linear system is asserted without its construction
statement: Known: a divisor whose translates x.D − D are all linearly equivalent lies in a bounded linear system with an action X × P → P (57/305-306): linearization of invertible sheaves under a connected group (Mumford, GIT, ch. 1 §3; Sumihiro 1974).

entry: C07 — A group-scheme immersion proof retains its characteristic restriction
statement: Known over a field in every characteristic: monomorphisms of algebraic groups are closed immersions (SGA 3, VI_B 1.4.2); the relative Proposition 7.2 with characteristic-zero residue fields (57/307) is as written.

entry: C10 — The Tribu leaves carry separate algebraic proof tasks
statement: Provenance: 57/299, 301, 303 are leaves of the reused "Tribu 43" typescript (heading dated October 1957); their tasks (p-bases, derivations, differential sequences) belong to that text, not to the Picard notes.

entry: Haar construction
statement: Edition: in the reused Haar-measure typescript (60/010, 008, 006, 004, read in that order) "que si μ = 0 et f = 0" is false and should read "ou" (one-point group); uniqueness is sent to "Chap. VII" and the text stops on 004 inside the invariance argument. Existence and uniqueness are known (Weil 1940; Bourbaki, Intégration VII).

entry: Heights, symbolic degree, and normalization
statement: Error of the reused exercises (60/024, 030): the degree defined by the least m with 𝔓^(m) ⊂ 𝔔 is not a length (cusp C = k[[t², t³]], 𝔔 = t⁴C: degree 3, length 4); so the printed criterion of ex. 1(b) rejects the principal ideal t⁴C, its generator choice fails for 𝔞 = 𝔪, y = t³, and the coefficient of ex. 2(d) inherits the defect.

entry: Additional separated exercise obligations
statement: Edition: in the reused commutative-algebra exercises of cote 60, "composante primaire de C" (60/022, ex. 4(b)) must mean a component of πC, and r is defined through ∧^{r+1}E with the variable k (60/032, ex. 23); the other items are standard exercise claims on the different, the conductor and pseudo-invertible ideals (Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative VII) and editorial notes on reused sheets (60/014, 018).

entry: A13 — Hom–tensor reflexivity is a projectivity test
statement: Known: E^* ⊗ E → End(E) reflexive (or onto) forces E projective (60/036-070, ex. 7): the dual-basis lemma; the note gives the proof.

entry: C07 — Problem055(a) asks for more than the averaging formula
statement: Known: Problem 055(a), "Dans les cas géométriques classiques, construire" the local factor data (60/045, 051, 055): local factors through inertia invariants and the monodromy filtration (Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem, Serre-Tate 1968; Deligne, Weil II, 1.8, in equal characteristic; SGA 7, IX for abelian varieties; Serre, Facteurs locaux, 1970); see @1478, @1479 and Michel Hua's project's 60-inertia-average-duality.

entry: S06 — Two free lattices are proposed as finite data for a reflexive lattice
statement: Known: a reflexive lattice is the intersection of its height-one localizations, hence M = L ∩ L_1 for suitable free lattices (60/068, ex. 3): Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative VII §4.

entry: A03 — Riemann–Roch needs the relative base-change step
statement: Known: h^0, h^1 of degree-n line bundles on genus-one fibres and their base change, "pour n=0 elle est connue par ailleurs" (62/005): cohomology and base change (EGA III 7; Mumford, Abelian Varieties §5; Stacks 0A1G).

entry: A04 — The omitted length-two separation argument
statement: Known: "un raisonnement connu n'utilisant que RR donne le résultat", very ampleness of nD for n ≥ 3 on genus-one fibres (62/005): degree ≥ 2g + 1 is very ample (Hartshorne IV 3.1; Stacks 0H2V).

entry: A05 — Universal injectivity and the exceptional degree one
statement: Universal injectivity of 𝓔_i ⊂ 𝓔_j for genus-one fibres, with the exclusion "n,m … ≠1" since 𝓔_1 = 𝓔_0 (62/006); standard (Katz-Mazur, ch. 2; Deligne, Courbes elliptiques: formulaire, 1975).

entry: A11 — The flex and tangent flag in the cubic embedding
statement: The origin and its "tangente d'inflexion" in the |3D|-embedding (62/009); standard.

statement: Edition: on 62/011 "Ici le discriminant s'explicite : -" is followed by no formula; the later "δ ≠ 0" must be read as δ a unit, and the y³ coefficient of the flex model must be a unit.

entry: A17 — Representability with a special basis
statement: Known: representability of "courbes elliptiques 'structurées'" by the coefficient scheme M (62/011-013): the Weierstrass atlas (Deligne, formulaire, 1975; Katz-Mazur 2.2; Stacks 072S).

entry: A19 — The promised general-genus argument is only a sketch
statement: Known: "un raisonnement général … pour les courbes de genre g" (62/013): M_g as a quotient of a Hilbert scheme of pluricanonically embedded curves (Mumford, GIT, ch. 5; Deligne-Mumford 1969).

entry: A22 — The expectation about the number of parameters
statement: "Il ne semble pas … moins de paramètres" (62/015): an expectation without a fixed class of presentations; the five-coefficient Weierstrass atlas is the standard characteristic-free presentation (Stacks 072S).

entry: A23 — Normalizing the discriminant by a finite flat cover
statement: A twelfth root of the unit discriminant gives a finite locally free cover, not étale over 2 and 3 (62/015); standard; the parenthesis "(…24.ième)" stays a reading question; variance as at @1554.

entry: A24 — Successive characteristic restrictions in normal forms
statement: Normal forms "en car ≠2, puis en car. ≠3, puis on verra" (62/015-016); standard (Weierstrass normal forms; Tate's formulaire).

entry: B15 — The degree-three quotient map and its uniqueness qualification
statement: The degree-three quotient map f(t) = F(t)/(3√−3 t(t−1)) and its normalizations (62/038); verified in the note; local.

entry: C02 — Why a trisection gives an S₃ torsor
statement: "classification dans un H¹(S, S₃)" of genus-zero curves with a trisection (62/042); standard descent (Stacks 04UV).

entry: C07 — Finiteness of normalization and the degree-three algebra
statement: Finiteness of the normalization in a degree-three étale algebra (62/046); standard (Stacks 032L); the everywhere-étale condition is the substantive one, see @1529, @1530.

entry: C11 — Invariant zero and the harmonic stabilizer
statement: Invariant zero and the harmonic stabilizer, "H¹(S, Z/2)" (62/048); on a reduced base standard; the nonreduced case is @1532.

entry: C14 — The intermediate double quotient and its quadratic cover
statement: The intermediate double quotient u ↦ iu² and the cover √i (62/048); local, verified in the note.

entry: C17 — The complete local example is an orbit description after a choice
statement: Known: "π₁(S)=0" for a complete local ring with algebraically closed residue field, and the orbit description after a choice (62/050): Stacks 04GK.

statement: Known: E complete, F separated, gr(u) surjective implies u surjective (62/026, Prop. 6): Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative III §2 no. 8.

statement: Known: at most n extensions of a valuation to a degree-n extension (62/031): Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative VI §8.

statement: Known: the integral closure is the intersection of the extension valuation rings, with the stated localizations (62/031): Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative VI §8; Serre, Corps locaux, I §4.

entry: A02 — The discriminant identity is asserted for a bare rank-two form
statement: The boxed identity Q_N(φ_N(x)) = −N(x)δ_N "sans autre donnée" for a rank-two quadratic module (84/098); discriminant-module algebra (Knus, Quadratic and Hermitian forms over rings, 1991, III; Voight 2016); the sign marked uncertain stays as read.

statement: The transpose i_A: 𝒜 → 𝒜_1 ⊗ 𝒜_2 "sans utiliser les structures de rev." (84/100); local.

statement: Known: the product of two quadratic algebras as the invariants of the diagonal involution when one factor is étale at each point of characteristic 2 (84/102): Knus 1991, III.4; Voight, Discriminants and the monoid of quadratic rings (2016); the note proves it on the cover D(2), D(b_1), D(b_2).

statement: Uniqueness of the norm with φ_N(ξ, η) = Tr(ξη̄) (84/105-106); local, verified in the note (A12).

statement: The contracted triple product is (A_1 ⊗ A_2 ⊗ A_3)^Γ away from characteristic-2 points with two non-étale factors (84/117); settled in the same notes (A30).

statement: "j'ai envie de prouver" that the constant map has values in k.1_A (84/118); part of #1264.

statement: The étale case of the three-cover proposition, "par twist" (84/119-121): Galois theory of (Z/2)²-torsors; part of #1264; the lemma's closed-subscheme hypothesis is @1567.

entry: A37 — The nonétale fibre construction is a stated program
statement: G.'s non-étale generalization (84/121, "J'ai envie de vérifier", "sans condition étale", "Ceci doit généraliser"): for quadratic algebras A_1, A_2, A_3 over k and a section ε of their contracted product A_1 * A_2 * A_3, prove or refute that the fibre π^{-1}(ε) of Spec(A_1 ⊗ A_2 ⊗ A_3) carries a biquadratic structure whose three quadratic subalgebras are the A_i, in the enlarged quasi-quadratic setting the next page's nonflatness warning requires; the étale case is the (Z/2)²-torsor classification.

statement: Functoriality of χ-split extensions, "c'est clair par construction", "Ça marche aussi" (84/126); local.

entry: N90-01 — The precise module criterion and its countability boundary
statement: Known: the saturated-hull criterion of Lemma 1 with "C'est aussi nécessaire si M a un ens. dénombrable de générateurs" (90/002): Pontryagin's criterion for countably generated torsion-free modules over a Dedekind ring; without countability the converse fails (Baer-Specker group Z^N).

entry: N90-04 — The strict projective-system assertion over a field
statement: Known: an affine group over a field is the projective limit of a strict projective system of algebraic quotients with faithfully flat transitions (90/006): Waterhouse, Introduction to affine group schemes, 3.3; Demazure-Gabriel III §3.

entry: N90-05 — Why the finite dual algebras matter

entry: N90-09 — The stable-hull programme over a general base
